const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/travel-app-notification-issue.md
+## Observed behavior
+
+Two state-changing paths commit their database transaction before writing the customer notification:
+
+- `app/actions.ts`, in `cancelBookingAction`, commits the booking cancellation, seat release, status history, and durable refund request before attempting `prisma.notification.create`.
+- `app/actions.ts`, in `updateFlightStatusAction`, commits the flight and booking status changes before attempting `prisma.notification.createMany`.
+
+Both notification writes catch and log failures without surfacing them. The underlying booking, flight, seat, and refund state can therefore commit while the corresponding in-app notification is absent.
+
+This was verified by reading the current source at `9407fd5`; it has not yet been reproduced by forcing a notification write failure against the running application.
+
+## Why it matters
+
+#76 requires customer, inventory, payment, and notification states to remain consistent. A customer can currently miss the only proactive notice that their booking was cancelled, disrupted, reinstated, or delayed even though the state transition succeeded.
+
+## Expected outcome
+
+- A committed cancellation or flight-status transition has a durable notification outcome.
+- Notification failure is explicit and recoverable rather than swallowed.
+- Delay notices still reach every affected customer even though a delay does not change `Booking.status`.
+- Deduplication preserves distinct outcomes for the same customer when multiple bookings are affected.
+- Tests cover notification-write failure as well as the successful self-service and staff-assisted paths.
+
+## Related work
+
+- #76 owns cancellation/disruption consistency.
+- #82 owns production-ready notification delivery and preferences.
+
+The implementation should decide between transaction-scoped in-app notification writes and a durable outbox before adding external delivery channels.
*** End Patch";
